result.topic_en: Pencil calculations converting derivatives from Cartesian (p,q) to polar coordinates (r, φ), Cauchy–Riemann-type complex relations, and derivatives of x, y, a, b with respect to a parameter α via chain-rule expressions in p and q.
result.transcription:
$dp = \cos\varphi\, dr - \sin\varphi\, r\,d\varphi$
$dq = \sin\varphi\, dr + \cos\varphi\, r\,d\varphi$
$dr = \cos\varphi\, dp + \sin\varphi\, dq$
$r\,d\varphi = -\sin\varphi\, dp + \cos\varphi\, dq$

$\frac{\partial u}{\partial p} = \cos\varphi \frac{\partial u}{\partial r} - \sin\varphi \frac{\partial u}{r\,\partial\varphi}$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial q} = +\sin\varphi \frac{\partial u}{\partial r} + \cos\varphi \frac{\partial u}{r\,\partial\varphi}$
$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial q^2}$ [?] $= \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial r^2} + \frac{1}{r^2}\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \varphi^2} + \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}$

[-$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial q^2} = \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial r^2} + \partial \frac{\frac{\partial u}{r\partial\varphi}}{r\partial\varphi}$-]
$\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial y}{\partial p} i = \frac{\partial y}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial x}{\partial q} i$ $\quad \frac{\partial a}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial b}{\partial p} i = \frac{\partial b}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial a}{\partial q} i$

$\frac{\partial x}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q$ , $\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}$ [?] $+ \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial p \partial p} p + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial q \partial p} q$ , $\frac{\partial x}{\partial p}$, $\frac{\partial x}{\partial q}$,
$\frac{\partial y}{\partial \alpha}$ ------ $\frac{\partial y}{\partial p}$, $\frac{\partial y}{\partial q}$
$\frac{\partial a}{\partial \alpha}$ ------ $\frac{\partial a}{\partial p}$, $\frac{\partial a}{\partial q}$
$\frac{\partial b}{\partial \alpha}$ ------ $\frac{\partial b}{\partial p}$, $\frac{\partial b}{\partial q}$

$\partial x$

$\frac{\partial x}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q$ $\quad -\frac{\partial y}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p + \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q$,
$\frac{\partial y}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p$ $\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial \alpha} + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p - \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q$

$+2 \frac{\partial x}{\partial \alpha}$ [?] $\left( \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p + \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q \right)$
$-2 \frac{\partial y}{\partial \alpha} \left( \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial p \partial \alpha} p + \frac{\partial^2 x}{\partial q \partial \alpha} q \right)$

$1, 2(n-1)(\nu-1)$ [?] $\quad 1, 0, 0$
$1, 2(n-1)$ [?] $\quad 1, 0$ [?]
$1, 2(n-1)(\nu-1), \; 1, 0$ [?]
$\left( \begin{matrix} 4 & 3 & 2 \end{matrix} \right)$ [?]
